name: Rick Jackson
incumbencyStatus: challenger — political outsider, no prior elected office

biography.currentRole: Chairman and CEO, Jackson Healthcare (Alpharetta, GA)
priorRoles: Founder, Giving Films (faith-based nonprofit film production)
biography.education: Attended David Lipscomb College (Nashville, TN) — did not finish; took courses at Georgia State University
biography.background: Self-described rags-to-riches story: grew up in Atlanta's Techwood Homes (nation's first public housing project), spent childhood in 5 foster homes and attended 13 schools. Built Jackson Healthcare into one of the largest healthcare staffing firms in the U.S., reporting $3B in annual revenue (2025), serving 5M+ patients in 1,300+ facilities nationwide. Describes himself as a 'million dollar Trump donor' and political outsider. No prior elected or appointed government experience.
biography.religion: Faith-based philanthropist; Giving Films produces movies with faith-based messages
biography.notablePhilanthropy: Championed Georgia legislation (passed) providing free college tuition, room, and board for former foster youth at public colleges and technical schools — claims this came at zero new cost to taxpayers. His companies and family foundation fund scholarships, housing, and support services for foster youth. Supports FaithBridge Foster Care.

campaignWebsite.notes: WebFetch unavailable; content reconstructed from search snippets and multiple news sources citing the site directly.

statedPositions.quote: Cut the state income tax in half within 4 years and work to eliminate it within 8 years
statedPositions.notes: Also phrased in launch coverage as: 'if we can't cut the state income tax in half and freeze property taxes, I won't run again' — treated as a firm pledge

statedPositions.quote: Freeze property taxes immediately to stop runaway assessments that price families out of their homes
statedPositions.notes: Listed as first priority on Action Plan page

statedPositions.quote: Use technology and AI to eliminate wasteful spending and improve services
statedPositions.notes: General efficiency framing; no specifics on which programs would be cut

statedPositions.quote: Freeze tuition, room, and board at public colleges and technical schools
statedPositions.notes: Paired with record of already passing foster youth tuition-free legislation

statedPositions.quote: Schools should exist to educate rather than indoctrinate. Rick will restore common sense and parental authority in Georgia classrooms.
statedPositions.notes: Anti-DEI, anti-woke framing; supports parental rights over curriculum

statedPositions.quote: Make Georgia the number one state in the nation for deporting criminal illegal immigrants
statedPositions.notes: Also described in launch coverage as pledging 'criminal deportations'

statedPositions.quote: Prohibit DEI programs in state government, public universities and classrooms; criminalize reverse discrimination
statedPositions.notes: Multiple news sources (Georgia Recorder, 11alive, WABE) confirm both the DEI ban and the 'criminalize reverse discrimination' pledge from campaign launch

statedPositions.quote: I grew up in places where law enforcement was the difference between safety and chaos. I will always stand with those who protect our communities.
statedPositions.notes: Pro-law enforcement values statement; no specific policy proposal cited

statedPositions.quote: Making supporting foster children a major cause of his life — and will continue to do so as governor
statedPositions.notes: Values statement backed by concrete legislative record on tuition bill

statedPositions.quote: Fight to make Georgia the most affordable state in America
statedPositions.notes: Homepage tagline level; operationalized through tax cuts and tuition freeze

votingRecord.notes: No prior elected office. No legislative voting record exists. All scoring must rely on stated campaign positions, business record, and donor/endorsement history.

endorsements.notes: $50M self-funded campaign commitment, including $40M advertising buy. Described as one of the largest self-funded gubernatorial campaign launches in Georgia history.

endorsements.type: not endorsed — Trump endorsed Burt Jones
endorsements.notes: Jackson is actively courting Trump's attention, running ads in DC and Palm Beach media markets 'aimed at an audience of one.' Jackson describes himself as 'million dollar Trump donor' and says he'll be 'Trump's favorite governor.' As of Feb 2026, Trump has NOT endorsed Jackson.

keyExchanges.quote: Couldn't name a single White House policy he disagrees with
keyExchanges.notes: Paraphrase from AJC reporting — Jackson was unable to identify any Trump policy he opposed, even as Trump tariffs increased costs for Georgia families and ACA cuts raised premiums

keyExchanges.quote: I'm entirely pro life. I support the bill we have here. As governor, I wouldn't change a thing, one way or the other.
keyExchanges.notes: Refers to Georgia's LIFE Act (6-week abortion ban / heartbeat bill signed by Kemp 2019). Explicit endorsement of status quo; no mention of exceptions.

majorOpponents.name: Burt Jones
majorOpponents.notes: Trump-endorsed incumbent Lt. Gov.; Jackson's main competition for MAGA base. Jackson sued Jones over campaign finance law regarding Jones's leadership committee (WBJ Leadership Committee, $15.9M balance). Federal judge issued TRO against Jones's committee Feb 2026.

majorOpponents.name: Brad Raffensperger
majorOpponents.notes: Contested 2020 election results against Trump; less MAGA-aligned

campaignContext.pollingSnapshot: Quantus Insights poll (Feb 2026, commissioned by Jackson campaign) showed Jackson at 33% leading field. Rasmussen (Feb 2026) also showed Jackson ahead. Both polls taken within 2-3 weeks of entry; high name-ID effect from $40M ad buy. Many undecided voters in field.
campaignContext.campaignFinanceLawsuit: Jackson sued Lt. Gov. Jones alleging Georgia's 2021 'leadership committee' statute gives incumbents unconstitutional fundraising advantage. Jackson's limit: $8,400/donor (primary). Jones's leadership committee had no cap. Federal TRO issued Feb 20, 2026, barring Jones's committee from fundraising or spending for his governor's race.

positionConflicts.conflict: Jackson built his fortune in healthcare staffing and markets himself as a healthcare industry leader, yet opposes Medicaid expansion that would expand coverage to hundreds of thousands of Georgians and potentially keep rural hospitals open. His opposition is consistent with the full GOP primary field but creates tension with his industry background.

Jackson said he couldn't name a single White House policy he disagrees with, even as Trump tariffs are reportedly costing Georgia families $1,200+ annually and ACA-related changes are raising premiums by $860+/month. His healthcare business background makes blanket support of policies harming healthcare affordability notable.
sources: AJC 'Why Rick Jackson says he'll be Trump's favorite governor'

evidenceSummary.overallConfidence: medium — Entered race late February 2026 as political newcomer with no voting record. Strong evidence on taxes, healthcare (Medicaid), abortion, DEI/education, and immigration. Genuine gaps on climate, housing, guns, and criminal justice specifics. Press access was limited at launch; deeper interview record not yet established.
evidenceSummary.notes: As a first-time candidate, Jackson has fewer scored axes than incumbents. Do NOT infer positions from party affiliation alone — flag climate, guns, housing, and sentencing as genuinely missing data. His most distinctive positions are: (1) income tax elimination pledge with explicit accountability mechanism, (2) Medicaid expansion opposition despite healthcare industry background, (3) 'criminalize reverse discrimination' pledge alongside DEI ban, (4) self-funded MAGA outsider framing competing directly with Trump's own endorsed candidate.
